correctness.rationale: For arbitrary \(k\ge1\) and every positive n, all 1-indices have even parity; hence even palindromes are only zeros, and the maximal zero run is \(3^{k-1}\). Two explicitly exhibited and demonstrably distinct nonzero central palindromes exist at every short odd length; C_k supplies a central palindrome at each long odd length. These lower witnesses total exactly |C_k| distinct nonempty palindromes, forcing exhaustive equality by the universal at-most-|w| bound. Direct palindrome-center enumeration agrees with canonical representatives for every n at k=1..8; the universal proof does not rely on computation.

originality.rationale: The direct exact finite lengthwise spectrum and representative classification differs from the pre-existing Cantor richness assertion, from ordinary infinite factor complexity, and from prefix palindromic decomposition length. Targeted research-record and scholarly searches yielded no implication-equivalent finite per-length classification. The conclusion is not that Cantor richness is new; that part is explicitly prior. Historical priority risk remains under alternate terminology and incomplete publisher access.
residual_risks: Glen et al. (2008) already proves infinite Cantor richness, making the total |C_k| an old consequence, not a new result.
A pre-existing finite length-by-length formula could have appeared under Sierpinski-word or automatic-word terminology, notwithstanding targeted negative searches.
Direct publisher access for Lü et al. (2016) failed; indexed sections were read but cannot certify the entire document lacks a related appendix.
Independence and priority have not been externally certified.

value.rationale: A complete, scale-sharp classification of a natural word-combinatorial invariant for every iterate of a standard automatic word, including all representatives and a cutover at the longest zero gap. The known rich-word total \(3^k\) does not specify distribution of palindromes by length or identify the unique long palindrome; this strengthens existing structure rather than computing another table.
